root_cause.text: In the pf1550 charger driver, `devm_request_threaded_irq()` was called before `devm_power_supply_register()`, so devm teardown could free/unregister the `power_supply` object before the IRQ handler was removed, allowing `pf1550_charger_irq_handler()` to call `power_supply_changed()` on a freed or not-yet-initialized handle.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the IRQ request loop from before `chg->charger = devm_power_supply_register(...)` to after it, and the CVE description explicitly says the reverse devm release order caused a race where an interrupt could fire after the `power_supply` was freed but before IRQ unregistration, leading to use-after-free in `power_supply_changed()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove probe-time charger IRQ registration from the PF1550 charger driver.
intent_record.what: The probe function `pf1550_charger_probe()` removes the entire loop that iterated over `PF1550_CHARGER_IRQ_NR`, fetched each IRQ with `platform_get_irq()`, stored it in `chg->virqs[i]`, and registered a threaded interrupt handler with `devm_request_threaded_irq()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the driver no longer requests or installs charger IRQ handlers during probe, so interrupt-driven charger event handling for those IRQ lines is disabled or deferred elsewhere. This also eliminates probe-time failures caused by missing IRQs or failed IRQ registration.

intent_record.intent_summary: Register and validate all PF1550 charger IRQs during probe so interrupt handling is available and initialization fails cleanly on IRQ setup errors.
intent_record.what: In pf1550_charger_probe(), a new loop was added before pf1550_dt_parse_dev_info() that iterates from i = 0 to PF1550_CHARGER_IRQ_NR - 1, retrieves each IRQ with platform_get_irq(pdev, i), stores it in chg->virqs[i], and registers a threaded interrupt handler with devm_request_threaded_irq() using pf1550_charger_irq_handler, IRQF_NO_SUSPEND, and the name "pf1550-charger". The probe now returns immediately on any IRQ lookup or request error.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the driver now actively acquires and handles all charger-related interrupts during probe instead of leaving them unregistered. This enables interrupt-driven charger event handling, and causes probe to fail early if any required IRQ is missing or cannot be requested, preventing the driver from initializing in a partially functional state.

The group changes IRQ registration during probe, which is directly tied to the root cause involving `devm_request_threaded_irq()` ordering relative to `devm_power_supply_register()`. Adjusting when and how IRQs are set up can prevent the handler from running before the power_supply is fully registered or after it is torn down.

candidates.rationale: This requests the charger IRQ during probe before the power_supply object is registered. With devm-managed teardown, the IRQ handler can outlive or race with the power_supply lifetime, leading to pf1550_charger_irq_handler() calling power_supply_changed() on an invalid handle.

This is the IRQ callback that can run before the power_supply is fully initialized or after it has been torn down, directly triggering the unsafe power_supply_changed() path described in the root cause.
Storing and using the IRQ before power_supply registration reflects the premature interrupt setup sequence that exposes the handler to a not-yet-registered or already-freed power_supply.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the probe-time IRQ registration that occurs before devm_power_supply_register(), creating the teardown ordering bug where the IRQ handler may run after the power_supply object has been freed or before it is fully initialized.
This is the IRQ handler associated with the prematurely registered interrupt; it can invoke power_supply_changed() on an invalid power_supply handle due to the lifetime mismatch.

This stores the IRQ during probe as part of the premature interrupt setup sequence, contributing to the handler being active before the power_supply registration and safe lifetime ordering are established.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable ordering is present in this probe function. The code requests IRQs first: `for (i = 0; i < PF1550_CHARGER_IRQ_NR; i++) { ... ret = devm_request_threaded_irq(&pdev->dev, irq, NULL, pf1550_charger_irq_handler, ...); }` and only later registers the power supplies: `chg->charger = devm_power_supply_register(&pdev->dev, &pf1550_charger_desc, &psy_cfg);` followed by `chg->battery = devm_power_supply_register(&pdev->dev, &pf1550_battery_desc, &psy_cfg);`. The IRQ handler/work path uses `power_supply_changed(chg->battery);` and `power_supply_changed(chg->charger);`, so if devm teardown unregisters the power_supply objects before the IRQ is removed, the handler can dereference stale handles. There is no fix in this snippet, because the registration order is still IRQs-before-power-supply and there is no added synchronization or teardown protection.
